summary.headline: Ajanta Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% to Rs 1,794 crore and PAT 49% to Rs 388 crore, but management guided to a weaker H2 on US and institutional normalisation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 33% to Rs 1,794 crore, EBITDA rose 47% to Rs 543 crore (30% margin) and PAT rose 49% to Rs 388 crore. Every business grew in the quarter, led by US generics (+41%), Africa branded generics (+41%) and Africa Institution (+259%), with Asia branded generics rebounding 18%. Management said H1 benefited from elevated US sales on a limited-competition product and an unusually strong institutional quarter, both of which will normalise in H2. FY27 guidance was retained at high-teens revenue growth, around 27% EBITDA margin and around 78% gross margin, with US growth guidance cut to high single digits from mid single digits.

financial_highlights.change: +34% YoY (from Rs 745 crore); reported H1 EBITDA Rs 971 crore, 28% margin after Rs 26 crore forex loss
Improvement over FY26 attributed mainly to favourable currency
Includes forex gain of Rs 24 crore (Q2) and Rs 69 crore (H1)
After interim dividend of about Rs 400 crore paid in the quarter
Q2 Rs 72 crore vs Rs 63 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Asia branded generics
segments.commentary: Q2 sales Rs 366 crore, +18% YoY from Rs 310 crore, after Rs 255 crore in Q1 due to logistics and supply-chain issues; H1 sales Rs 621 crore, +1%. Four new products launched in H1.

segments.name: Africa branded generics
segments.commentary: Q2 sales Rs 312 crore, +41% YoY; H1 Rs 607 crore, +35%. Drivers cited were market share gains, new launches (three in H1), field force additions and favourable currency.

segments.name: US generics
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 484 crore, +41% YoY; H1 Rs 971 crore, +49%, supported by a limited-competition product with a lower base. Three launches, four final approvals and one ANDA filed in H1; 17 ANDAs pending. FY27 growth guidance cut to high single digits.

segments.name: Africa Institution
segments.commentary: Q2 sales Rs 116 crore, +259% YoY; H1 Rs 187 crore, +164%. Management does not expect H1 levels to be sustained in H2 given unpredictable institutional procurement.

segments.name: India branded business
segments.commentary: Q2 sales Rs 504 crore, +16% YoY; H1 Rs 1,013 crore, +20%. IQVIA MAT Sept 2026 growth 17% vs market 13%; rank improved to 23rd from 24th. Cardiology 37%, ophthalmology 28%, dermatology 22%, pain 10%, newer areas 3% of India sales. Trade generics Rs 56 crore in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance unchanged at high teens, with H2 moderating as US competition builds and institutional sales normalise.
US generics full-year growth guidance revised to high single digits from mid single digits earlier.
Asia branded generics full-year growth guided to mid-teens; Africa branded generics guided to high double digits, with H2 momentum expected to be slightly lower but robust.
India guidance mid-teens; management expects to grow 20-25% faster than IPM in the covered market, with a firmer view after Q3.

Gross margin about 78% (plus or minus 100 bps) for FY27; EBITDA margin about 27% (plus or minus 100 bps), implying H2 margin below H1 (about 26% per analyst back-calculation, confirmed directionally by management).
R&D about 5% of revenue for FY27, with spending stepping up in H2; effective tax rate about 26.5%.
Capex about Rs 400 crore for FY27, including about Rs 150 crore maintenance; Rs 210 crore spent in H1.
Other expenses expected to remain broadly aligned with current trend.
Working capital: receivable days to improve further, inventory days to return to March 2026 levels by year-end.
Semaglutide in-licensing: sales expected to begin in FY28 and trickle in over time, given about 2-year average registration lead time; contribution to be included in future annual guidance.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at about Rs 400 crore, of which about Rs 150 crore is maintenance and the balance is capacity expansion; Rs 210 crore spent in H1.
Emerging-markets MR strength at about 2,500 after adding about 100 in H1 (from 2,400); guidance is for 7-8% field-size growth over FY27.
US R&D programme runs more than 15-20 complex products at a time (more than 50% of portfolio is DR/ER); target 8-10 ANDA filings per year, versus 5-7 mentioned earlier in the call.
India MR productivity (PCPM) improved to Rs 4.5 lakh in H1 FY27 from Rs 3.7 lakh in FY26.
Emerging-markets productivity stated at about Rs 8 lakh and above.
demand_pricing: US: H1 growth was supported by a limited-competition product; new competitors have entered and management expects share and sales to normalise in H2.
Institutional Africa: procurement is lumpy in timing and value; management does not expect H1 levels to continue in H2.
India: IPM growth strong at 12-13% in H1, attributed to hospital bed-to-patient ratio improvement, government schemes, insurance coverage and a slowdown in unbranded generics.
Asia: logistics via alternate shipping routes and supply-chain normalisation helped; some Q1 sales pushed into Q2-Q4.
Currency: management cited a 4-5% currency gain across export business (possibly higher), which aided gross margin and Africa growth.
NLEM price-control exposure: management said oncology-only, so zero impact on Ajanta; no specific product list yet for cardiology.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the 49% H1 US growth: launches, share gains or pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a limited-competition product that stayed at elevated sales through Q1 and Q2 FY27; new competitors have now entered, so sales are expected to normalise in H2. US guidance cut to high single digits.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 EBITDA margin around 26% given the 27% guidance and 29% H1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO confirmed H2 margin will be lower than H1, as US competition builds, institutional sales normalise and R&D and field-force spend step up.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cardiology growth lower than IPM in IQVIA data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is in line with or slightly better than the covered market; an anomaly in IQVIA data is being resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 4-5% currency gain and H1 forex loss affect profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q2 had no forex loss but a gain; H1 had a Rs 26 crore loss in other expenses and a Rs 69 crore gain in other income, for a net H1 gain of Rs 43 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital improve further by March 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said receivables may improve further, but inventory days will revert to around March 2026 levels at year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of NPPA/NLEM drug-pricing moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the products under NLEM review are oncology-only, so there is no impact; no product list yet for cardiology, so no immediate threat.

qa_highlights.question: When will the semaglutide in-licensing contribute to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales expected from FY28, trickling in across many countries because registration takes about 2 years on average; dossiers only recently filed.

risks_watch: H2 FY27 slowdown in US generics as new competitors enter the limited-competition product.
Lumpy Africa institutional procurement; management does not expect H1 levels to sustain.
EBITDA margin trending to around 26% in H2, below the 27% guided full-year level.
Asia recovery depends on logistics normalisation and catch-up of pushed-out Q1 sales.
Possible future NLEM/price-control expansion into cardiology; management says no specific list yet.
Forex: H1 benefited from currency tailwinds (gross margin and Africa growth); reversal would hit margins.
Semaglutide in-licensing revenue timing from FY28 and dependent on country registrations.
Reconciling IQVIA cardiology data discrepancy noted by management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H1 delivery and the India and Africa franchises, but deliberately cautious on H2, explicitly flagging US competition, institutional normalisation and higher R&D and field-force spend. Management declined to give geography-wise margins, MR splits by region or specialty, and FY28 guidance, which limited detail on several questions.
key_quotes: We remain confident of maintaining an EBITDA margin of around 27% with a variation of plus or minus 100 basis points, while continuing to invest in the development of our market.
This implies a lower margin in the second half than in the first as competition in the US builds, institutional sales normalize and we step up investment in R&D and our field force.
So, for the whole year, Asia, we are looking to post a mid-teens kind of growth.
Our growth is in line with the IPM. As I have mentioned in the presentation also, there is some anomaly in the IQVIA numbers which we are trying to sort out, but I think it is taking some time.

I think it will come to the similar level. In receivables you may see some improvement, but in inventory we will go back to the March level because currently half year and quarter end, so some down, but I think year end, you expect the same like what last year we have closed.
